title: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head K (Ministry of Education)

sections.label: Abolish streaming and GEP
sections.summary: The speaker recommends abolishing streaming in favour of SBB and scrapping the Gifted Education Programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In 2004, MOE decided to merge the EM1 and EM2 steams and, in 2008, announced that the EM3 academic stream will be scrapped.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I, therefore, recommend that streaming be abolished and replaced by SBB for both academic and non-academic subjects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Next, the second sacred cow – Gifted Education Programme (GEP).

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I think it should be scrapped if SBB can be introduced.

sections.label: Abolish GEP, cluster students
sections.summary: The speaker says GEP should be abolished and students clustered in subject-banded academic programmes that suit them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: GEP should be abolished and students who excel in specific subjects or learn differently can be clustered in subject-banded academic programmes that suit them.

sections.label: Pilot 10-year through train
sections.summary: The speaker urges piloting a 10-year through train from Primary 1 to remove the PSLE high-stakes exam.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Even with the latest removal of exams in Primary 1 and Primary 2 and some transitional years, parents and others in society are not blind to the fact that there is still a high-stakes exam at the end of six years of the primary school education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, there are good reasons why we should seriously pilot a 10-year through train system from Primary 1 and slay the PSLE sacred cow: (a) it removes the unnecessary step of prematurely sorting children through a high-stakes exam at the age of 12, many of whom are still developing; and (b) removing PSLE frees up substantive PSLE preparation time which are often hot-housing time to crunch a few selected academic subjects, such as English, Mathematics and Science, which do not reflect a holistic education.

sections.label: Shadow $1 billion tuition industry
sections.summary: The speaker says MOE should not ignore the shadow $1 billion education industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: MOE should not ignore this elephant in the room and be resigned to this shadow $1 billion education industry.

sections.label: Slay five sacred cows
sections.summary: The speaker seeks the Ministry's consideration to examine and consider slaying five sacred cows: Streaming, GEP, Competitions, PSLE and Tuition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But new online on-demand tutoring platforms have already started in the tuition industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I believe that if MOE puts its heart to it, it can find ways by which it can take on the tuition industry and remove the excesses of the over-reliance on tuition, especially for students who do not need it.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Ms Denise Phua, can you round up your speech?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: I, therefore, seek the Ministry's consideration to examine, diagnose and consider slaying the five sacred cows I have mentioned today – Streaming, GEP, Competitions, PSLE and Tuition.

sections.label: Expand SBB, blur streams
sections.summary: The speaker suggests MOE expand SBB further to blur the distinction between Normal and Express Stream students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Students doing SBB had done well and, clearly, SBB has shown that, sometimes, we pigeonhole and stream our young too early.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: They have potential which can be unleashed through avenues like SBB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Thus, I would like to suggest that MOE seriously consider expanding SBB further to blur the distinction between the Normal and Express Stream students.

sections.label: Replacing secondary school streams
sections.summary: Asks whether the Minister would replace the Express, Normal (Academic) and Normal (Technical) streams with an alternative recognising wider abilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong (Punggol East)
sentences.text: Would the Minister consider replacing the Express, Normal (Academic) and Normal (Technical) Streams for our secondary schools with an alternative which recognises a wider range of abilities to better cater for the unique strengths and interests of students and help build our students' confidence and develop an intrinsic motivation to learn for life?

sections.label: Abolishing secondary streaming for SBB
sections.summary: Asks if MOE will abolish secondary streaming and focus solely on SBB, as in primary schools, noting streaming began in 1979 and 1980.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will MOE consider abolishing streaming in secondary schools and focus solely on SBB, which is what we are doing in the primary schools?

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Academic streaming was first introduced in our mainstream primary schools in 1979 and in our mainstream secondary schools in 1980 under the then New Education System as a result of the Report on MOE published in 1978, or what is popularly known as the Goh Report.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It has been 40 years since we started streaming our students in schools according to their academic abilities – into Normal Bilingual, Extended Bilingual or Monolingual Streams in primary school, and the Gifted, Special/Express, Normal (Academic) (NA) or Normal (Technical) (NT) streams in secondary school.

sections.label: Repeated calls to abolish streaming
sections.summary: States the speaker has spoken about academic streaming many times and each time called for its abolition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To this day, those words are still so vivid.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I have spoken about academic streaming many times before in this Chamber and, each time, I have called for us to abolish academic streaming.

sections.label: Reconsidering academic streaming and labels
sections.summary: Says with multiple pathways and SBB it is time to reconsider academic streaming and remove labels causing self-limiting beliefs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With our recognition of the multiple pathways to the different peaks of excellence, and with the implementation of SBB for differentiated teaching and learning, and ability-based pedagogies, it is time to reconsider academic streaming and look at ways in which we can remove the academic streams and, more importantly, remove these labels that lead to self-limiting beliefs and self-fulfilling prophecies.

sections.label: Express requirement for specialised schools
sections.summary: Implores the Ministry to reconsider the Express stream academic requirement for students admitted to Specialised Independent Schools, Sports School and SOTA.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On a related note, I would like to once again implore the Ministry to reconsider the Express stream academic requirement for students admitted into the Specialised Independent Schools, the Sports School and School of the Arts (SOTA).

sections.label: Broadening school and IHL admissions
sections.summary: Says MOE cannot ban tuition but can realign focus and review admissions to look beyond high-stakes examination results.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: MOE cannot ban tuition or eradicate similar practices in the private sector, which is driven by consumer demand.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But what the MOE can do is to realign the focus on achievement and personal development rather than attainment alone.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Admission requirements to our schools and IHLs need to continue to be reviewed and expanded to look beyond the results of high stakes examinations alone.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Admission to secondary schools can incorporate student portfolios in addition to their PSLE results, while admission to IHLs should continue to look at the applicants’ community contribution, prior work experience, co-curricular involvement or leadership skills, beyond their GCE or other similar high-stakes examination results.

sections.label: JC merger site choices
sections.summary: The passage notes Yishun and Pioneer JCs were chosen as merger sites in 2019 and asks whether the old Jurong JC site would be better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: When Yishun and Innova JCs were merged in 2019, the chosen site was Yishun JC, which is older with aged facilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: When Jurong and Pioneer JCs were merged in 2019, the chosen site was Pioneer JC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: However, the site of the old Jurong JC will be near to a new Mass Rapid Transit station when the Jurong Regional Line opens in 2026 which, in that case, would improve the connectivity for the students who are studying at the site of old Jurong JC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Would not the old Jurong JC site be a better site?

sections.label: Upgrading older JCs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MOE plans to upgrade junior colleges that are more than 20 or 30 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Does MOE have plans to upgrade the JCs which are more than 20 or 30 years old?

sections.label: Insufficient school AEDs
sections.summary: The passage states AED numbers are grossly insufficient, averaging one to two in primary schools, with many secondary schools having none.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: The number of AEDs is grossly insufficient, with an average of one to two in all primary schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Many secondary schools do not even have any AED.

sections.label: SEN support in IHLs
sections.summary: The passage says unless the Government insists SEN support is fundamental, Singapore's IHLs may be perceived as less than first-world in this aspect.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Unless the Government, the key funder of education, insists that SEN support is an important fundamental feature of a progressive educational system, Singapore may belong to the first-world economically but its IHLs, in this aspect, will be perceived as less than first-world.

sections.label: Inconsistent support and recommendations
sections.summary: The passage states structured support is inconsistent across institutions in course selection, project work, internships and career guidance, and lists eight recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: There is also inconsistent structured support across these institutions in course selection, project work, internships and career guidance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: There are eight recommendations I would like to make for the schools and IHLs.

sections.label: More specialist SEN support
sections.summary: The passage calls for increasing access to specialist support from MOE and disability VWOs and setting up an MOE-level support function for IHLs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Increase availability and access to more specialist support from MOE and disability voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs).

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: And, especially for the IHLs, set up a support function at the MOE level to ensure the proper resourcing and support of these students.

sections.label: Government-funded specialised schools
sections.summary: Examples include Government-funded schools for Special Stream or Normal (T) Stream students and for students gifted in sports or the arts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: Examples include schools meant for students who qualify for the Special Stream or Normal (T) Stream only, and schools meant for students who are gifted in sports or the arts, all with Government funding.

sections.label: Support for mild special needs
sections.summary: Mainstream school admission of students with mild special needs remains low, and MOE is asked for more funding and trained personnel.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: While our mainstream schools have made strides in admitting students with mild special needs, these numbers are still relatively low.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: Will MOE be able to provide more funding support and the provision of more trained teaching and support personnel, such as AEDs or subject teachers trained in Special Needs Teaching, in our mainstream schools so that they can be more inclusive towards students with mild special needs?

sections.label: Teachers trained for ITE students
sections.summary: The passage asks how many teachers are trained to cope with the learning needs of these ITE students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How many teachers do we have who are trained to cope with the learning needs of these ITE students?

sections.label: Young man withdrew from polytechnic
sections.summary: The young man withdrew from the polytechnic because of the escalation of an incident.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, the young man withdrew from the polytechnic because of the escalation of an incident.

sections.label: Skills Council for persons with SEN
sections.summary: It proposes a Skills Council for Persons with SEN to develop a Lifelong CET System and appoint special schools as training centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: One, set up a Skills Council for Persons with SEN.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: This council should comprise MOE's SSG and SPED units, SG Enable, Workforce Singapore (WSG), the Employment and Employability Institute and the top VWOs representing the major disability groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: It should develop a Lifelong Continuing Education and Training (CET) System for Persons with Special Needs that will be regularly updated and extend the curriculum framework currently used during the SPED school years with a good balance of academic, vocational and lifeskills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Second, appoint promising special schools with track records to set up training centres in their locations to provide the identified training solutions for SPED graduands in the major disability groups.

sections.label: Guidelines for School-Home Partnership
sections.summary: Home, school and community partnership had been informal, and the Ministry launched Guidelines for School-Home Partnership suggesting actions for parents and schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So far, the partnership between homes, schools and communities had been informal and not so structured.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I am pleased to note that the Ministry had recently launched a set of Guidelines for School-Home Partnership which suggest actions that parents and schools can take to help our children develop their self-management skills.

sections.label: Youth mental health statistics
sections.summary: The passage states rates of youth suicides, help-seeking and depression in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, there was one to two suicides a month in 2016 among those aged 10 to 19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The number of young Singaporeans seeking help for mental health issues jumped by 190% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Depression affects up to 18% of youths in Singapore.

sections.label: Mental health treatment gap
sections.summary: The 2016 Singapore Mental Health Study found the treatment gap narrowed from 82.1% in 2010 to 78.4% in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Encouragingly, the 2016 Singapore Mental Health Study found a narrowing in the treatment gap, noting a decrease in the percentage of those not seeking help from 82.1% in 2010 to 78.4% in 2016.

sections.label: Mandating school mental health education
sections.summary: The passage calls for mandatory mental health education in schools and IHLs plus support for parents and families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mandating mental health education in our schools and IHLs is the surest signal to normalise mental health, together with providing support structures for parents and families to be equipped with emotional management skills, coping mechanisms and problem-solving skills to help our children and youths better navigate stress.

sections.label: Third Language and CCA places
sections.summary: The passage discusses the Malay Third Language programme, ASEAN economies, and limited CCA places for Physical Sports and Arts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the Ministry's reply to my PQ on this programme in September 2018, I quote, "The objective of the programme is to nurture a segment of non-Malays in each generation who are comfortably conversant in the Malay Language and able to engage with regional countries effectively." Under the current setting, only Malay and Bahasa Indonesia are offered as a Third Language.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was also said by the Ministry that apart from learning languages, I quote "students also have the opportunity to experience school-based enrichment modules on understanding Southeast Asia and participate in learning journeys as well as take part in cultural camps and immersion trips to Southeast Asian countries." Sir, in Minister Heng Swee Keat's Budget speech, he shared that the 10 economies of ASEAN are projected to become the fourth largest in the world by 2030 and that working together with ASEAN nations can maximise our potential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Heading towards 2030 where ASEAN is projected to be the fourth largest economy in the world, I believe the inclusion of other ASEAN languages in the RSP will be timely and a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: As MOE has stated, "CCAs also promote friendships among students from diverse backgrounds as they learn, play and grow together." Students can choose the CCA of their choice, but I understand that for "Physical Sports" and "Visual and Performing Arts Group" CCAs, places are often limited and given to those who do well in those areas and can represent the school.

sections.label: CCA places for all students
sections.summary: The passage asks what plans the Ministry has to ensure CCA places are available to all students, not just school representatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Can Minister share what plans the Ministry has to ensure that places for CCAs are available to all students and not just those who represent the school in competitions?

sections.label: CCAs at division level
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MOE can consider organising certain CCAs at division, GRC or district level.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can MOE consider organising certain CCAs at the division, Group Representation Constituency or even district level?

sections.label: MOE recognition of CCA involvement
sections.summary: Asks whether MOE can recognise this involvement as an official CCA.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can MOE recognise this involvement as their official CCA?

sections.label: Polytechnic intake limit increase
sections.summary: Polytechnic intake limit rose from 2.5% to 12.5% due to overwhelming response.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For polytechnics, the limit for intake was increased from 2.5% to 12.5% due to overwhelming response.

sections.label: EAE dropout and course-switch statistics
sections.summary: Asks whether statistics exist on EAE students who drop out or switch courses midway.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Are there statistics on the number of EAE students who drop out or switch courses midway?

sections.label: Fairness of EAE testing procedures
sections.summary: Asks how the fairness of EAE testing procedures and outcomes can be ensured.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: How can the fairness of EAE testing procedures and outcomes be ensured?

sections.label: ITE graduates under JPAE admissions
sections.summary: Says ITE graduates are perceived as admitted only after remaining vacancies under JPAE, and the system needs tweaking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Under the Joint Polytechnic Admissions Exercise (JPAE), the ITE graduates are seen as, or at least that is the public perception, that they are given admission only after any remaining vacancies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: We need to address this and tweak the system so that ITE graduates are not only treated as equals but also seen to be treated as equals under the admissions exercise.

sections.label: Autonomous university endowment ranges
sections.summary: States AU endowments range from about $400 million to about $4 billion, and per undergraduate from about $28,000 to more than $400,000.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: AU endowments range from about $400 million for the Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT) and the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) to about $4 billion dollars for the National University of Singapore (NUS).

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On a per undergraduate basis, this ranges from about $28,000 at SUSS to more than $400,000 at the Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD).

sections.label: 75th percentile salary range
sections.summary: The 75th percentile ranged from $3,000 for SUSS to about $4,000 for NUS.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The 75th percentile ranged from $3,000 for SUSS to about $4,000 for NUS.

sections.label: $3.6 billion worker training fund
sections.summary: An amount of $3.6 billion has been set aside over the next three years to help workers adapt to changes and acquire new skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: An amount of $3.6 billion has been set aside over the next three years to help workers adapt to changes and acquire new skills.

sections.label: Training subsidies beneficiaries and survey
sections.summary: 465,000 Singaporeans from 12,000 enterprises benefited from training subsidies, and a survey of 3,500 trainees found 80% found training helpful.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Based on the latest figures from SSG, 465,000 Singaporeans from 12,000 enterprises have benefited from training subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: A recent survey of 3,500 trainees indicated that 80% of them found the training helpful.

sections.label: Structured partnership model for training roadmaps
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to consider a structured partnership model to determine key training roadmaps by industry sector, clustered along the 23 Industry Transformation Maps.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: First, perhaps the Minister can consider developing a structured partnership model to determine key training roadmaps by industry sector, perhaps clustered along the 23 Industry Transformation Maps.

sections.label: Lead Training Provider with SIC
sections.summary: A Lead Training Provider is proposed to partner SIC in developing the skills and certification framework and practice-based training programmes customised to the sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, appoint a Lead Training Provider (LTP) to partner SIC in developing the skills and certification framework and practice-based training programmes, highly customised to meet the skills and competencies required in the sector.

sections.label: LTP mandate review and technologies
sections.summary: The LTP mandate could be reviewed every five years, and many technologies can improve productivity but demand fundamental changes in how work is done.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Perhaps, their mandate as LTP is subject to review, say, every five years, to keep the sector dynamic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: There are many technologies available that can improve productivity by helping workers to do things cheaper, better and faster, but they also demand fundamental changes in the way that work is done in organisations.

sections.label: CET demand in polytechnics
sections.summary: Constant reskilling amid company transformation will raise demand for CET opportunities in polytechnics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With the need to reskill constantly to keep up with the demands of the job as companies undergo structural and business transformation, there will be a higher demand for CET opportunities in our polytechnics.

sections.label: Effectiveness of SSG courses
sections.summary: Given investment in SSG, we must better understand how effective SSG courses have been for motivated individuals.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Given the considerable investment in SSG at both the national and individual levels, we must seek to better understand how effective SSG courses have been for individuals with a genuine motivation to upgrade themselves.

sections.label: Private providers and SSG fraud
sections.summary: Private providers offer SSG courses, but fraud cases have marred perceptions, and underprivileged families need support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: Our private education providers – whether it is the Private Education Institutions (PEIs) or other private organisations – have also come on board the SSG national movement and offer a slew of creative and interesting courses, both formal programmes and CET.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: However, several cases of fraud by private organisations and some PEIs with regard to SSG training provision have marred the perception of PEIs and other private organisations that provide SSG training or certification.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
sentences.text: While we recognise the central role of the family in ensuring that our young grow up well with desirable values, and that our old can age well and live a meaningful life in their golden years, we cannot underestimate the effect of inadequate support that underprivileged or low-income families receive.

sections.label: Support for disadvantaged students
sections.summary: It asks whether the task force identified disadvantaged students' main issues and what strategies can support them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: In particular, has the task force identified the main issues faced by the disadvantaged students?

sentences.speaker: Mr Charles Chong
sentences.text: And are there any strategies that we can pursue to better support these students?

sections.label: Post-secondary education completion rate
sections.summary: Minister Heng Swee Keat said nine in 10 persons have completed post-secondary education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Minister Heng Swee Keat, in his Budget round-up speech last week made the point that, currently, nine in 10 persons have completed post-secondary education.

sections.label: UPLIFT for disadvantaged children
sections.summary: Meritocracy left some families behind, so UPLIFT was set up to support underperforming children from disadvantaged homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: This task, however, would not be easy, as generations of families have already taken advantage of our meritocratic system to forge ahead, leaving behind families which have more serious issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: It is in this context that I had welcomed the Government’s announcement in November last year that it has set up UPLIFT, headed by the hon Minister Indranee Rajah, to find meaningful ways to support children from disadvantaged homes who are underperforming.

sections.label: Secondary school absenteeism report
sections.summary: A media report said that in 2017, 7.5 secondary school students out of every 1,000 were absent 60 days or more without a valid reason.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: One media report said that in 2017, 7.5 secondary school students out of every 1,000 were absent for 60 days or more without a valid reason.

sections.label: SHATEC formal education requirement
sections.summary: SHATEC said they required 10 years of formal education, which he did not have.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: SHATEC said they required 10 years of formal education, which he did not have.

sections.label: Girl returned to school
sections.summary: Worried she would drop out, they contacted primary and secondary school principals, found her schoolmates and got her back to school in mid-February.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: From my earlier experience with the boy, I was worried that she, too, would drop out of school as well.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: We contacted both the primary and secondary school principals and managed to find the schoolmates that she knew and got her back to school in mid-February.

sections.label: Counselling dropouts and preschool question
sections.summary: Secondary education is not compulsory but students who want to drop out or have high absenteeism must be counselled and helped, and he asked if MOE intends to make preschool education compulsory.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: While secondary education is not compulsory, it is crucial that we really counsel and help the students who want to drop out or have high absenteeism.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: I would also like to ask if MOE intends to make preschool education compulsory.

sections.label: Tampines primary schools programme
sections.summary: Today, the programme is going strong with seven Tampines primary schools participating in it.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: Today, the programme is going strong with seven Tampines primary schools participating in it.

sections.label: Handover from primary to secondary
sections.summary: He asked how MOE ensures a proper handover of students like Jess from primary to secondary school.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: Furthermore, how does MOE ensure that there is a proper handover of these students like Jess from primary to secondary school?

sections.label: Saranya and Jurong assistance scheme
sections.summary: Saranya's father is the sole breadwinner earning under $1,000 monthly, and she joined the Jurong Central Student Assistance Scheme receiving $50 monthly vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Her father is the sole breadwinner in the family and is earning less than $1,000 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: I met Saranya during one of the events in the Jurong Community Club when she narrated her situation to me.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng

sentences.text: Third, there are many causes of inequality, not just a single cause: from differences at birth in people's abilities, to differences in resources that parents can invest in their children; from differences in educational outcomes, to the way technology and market forces shape wages of different groups of Singaporeans; from the difficulties and derailers that life's circumstances present, to issues of individual motivation and mindset; from lack of awareness about help schemes and support services, to challenges in navigating the system and accessing these opportunities and schemes.

sections.summary: The Member asks how many community or grassroots-initiated after-school care centres exist and whether CATCH Plus can be supported or taken over.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Can I ask the Minister how many community or grassroots-initiated after-school care centres there are in the community, and whether she could support or even take over CATCH Plus?

sections.label: Community after-school SCC facilities
sections.summary: SCC is an after-school facility outside the school curriculum, where the school provides premises and works with others such as the Big Heart Centre.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And then, there are things which can be done in the community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, the SCC, which is after school, is really a facility that is provided outside of the school curriculum.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For that, what the school does is that the school provides the premises, and the school works with others to provide the programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, the Big Heart Centre, for example, was one of those; that is, the three self-help groups that have come together to provide services, and they work together with the school.

sections.label: CATCH Plus programme
sections.summary: The CATCH Plus programme referred to by the Member is stated to be a very good programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The CATCH Plus programme that the Member referred to is actually a very good programme.

sections.label: Mandating mental health education
sections.summary: The Member asks whether mental health education will be mandated as part of health education requirements in schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: Right now, we know that health education is compulsory but it is confined to physical health education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: Will we be looking at mandating mental health education as part of health education requirement in schools, so that our children know from a young age that both aspects of their well-being are equally important?

sections.label: ITE students and universities
sections.summary: Many countries view it as resembling their universities, and ITE students pay only 3% of the total cost of delivery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: There are many countries that look at it and think this looks like their universities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Also, ITE students pay only 3% of the total cost of delivery.

sections.label: Separate queue for O level students
sections.summary: They come after GCE O level students, in a separate queue with separate places set aside for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: They do come after the GCE "O" levels students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But it is a separate queue with their separate places set aside for them.
